title: Payment gateway for Shopify: Which one fits your store?
summary: Compare 7 payment gateways for Shopify in the UAE based on the setup, standard pricing, payout timelines, broader payment options, and more.

One provider could take longer than expected to approve your account, then turn out to be so complicated to set up that you need to hire a developer. If the rest of your store is ready, that can push your launch back even further.


Another could support plenty of payment methods overall, but not the ones you actually need through its Shopify integration.


Now that Shopify Payments has reached the UAE, it might seem like the obvious answer… but availability is still limited. It’s currently in early access, so only certain merchants can use it.²


Suffice it to say, the payment gateways that come up most often in your research won’t always match exactly what your store needs.

## What to look for in a Shopify payment gateway in the UAE


Finding a payment gateway provider in the UAE that works with Shopify isn’t too hard.


The trickier part is finding one that works for your Shopify setup and day-to-day operations.


Another thing to consider is your onboarding timeline: once your Shopify store has been set up, you probably want to get set up with a payment gateway as soon as possible.


First things first, let’s start with the #1 must-have for your UAE Shopify payment gateway provider:


### Make sure it actually fits your Shopify setup and plan


When a provider says it integrates with Shopify, that can mean a few different things.


The integration might only be available in certain countries. And depending on the provider, it could appear directly in Shopify’s payment settings, require an app or plugin, or need a more technical setup.


Before you sign up, confirm:


- Is the solution available to businesses registered in the UAE?


- Does it offer a current, actively maintained Shopify app or plugin?


- Will you need a developer to get it live?


- Does the integration work with your current Shopify plan?


- Which features and payment methods does its Shopify integration support?


### Look for pricing that works with your margins


The first transaction or processing fee you come across from a potential provider won’t always give you the full story.


Depending on your provider and Shopify plan, the total cost can include a percentage fee, a fixed amount per payment, international card or currency conversion charges, monthly account fees, setup costs, and refund or dispute fees. If you use an external provider, Shopify’s own third-party transaction fee sits on top of the provider’s processing charges.¹


Once you add everything up, the option that looked cheapest can end up costing more than you expected.


To get a fuller pricing picture, compare each provider using your usual order value:


- What will a typical domestic AED order cost?


- How much extra will you pay for an international card or non-AED payment?


- After all payment fees are deducted, how much of the sale do you keep?


### Check how international payments work


If your customers happen to buy from outside the UAE, check which currencies are available through the provider’s Shopify integration.


You should also confirm:


- What exchange rate applies


- Any conversion fees you’ll pay


- Which currency actually reaches your wallet or bank account


This tells you what customers abroad will see at checkout and what accepting their payments will really cost you.


### Find out when you’ll receive the money from your sales


A completed Shopify order doesn’t always mean you can withdraw your money right away. Your provider still has to process the payment, settle it, and send the funds to you. But to maintain your stock, you ideally need fast access to that cash – especially during the early days.


Check:


- How long settlement usually takes


- How often payouts are sent


- Whether weekends or public holidays can slow things down


- Whether new accounts start with longer payout timelines


- If faster payout or cashout options are available, what they cost, and who qualifies


Now that you know what to look for, let’s take a closer glance at what each option has to offer.

## Shopify Payments


Shopify Payments keeps payment setup, management, and reporting inside Shopify for eligible Shopify Plus merchants.


Because it’s Shopify’s own payment provider, you can activate and manage it through your Shopify admin, view payout reporting in the same place, and avoid Shopify’s third-party transaction fee on orders processed solely through Shopify Payments.¹


In the UAE, Shopify Payments supports major credit and debit cards, Shop Pay, Apple Pay, and Google Pay.³ You can receive payouts in AED to an eligible local bank account, and Shopify also documents USD payouts through its multi-currency payout setup.⁴


Note:


Shopify Payments is still in early access in the UAE and currently limited to eligible Shopify Plus merchants.² It’s also currently available for online selling only in the UAE, so in-person payments require an external terminal and third-party processor.³


Could be a fit if:


You already use Shopify Plus, qualify for UAE early access, and want checkout, payment management, and reporting to stay closely connected to Shopify.


## Stripe


Stripe could make sense if Shopify is only one part of a broader online payment setup.


It’s a global payment platform used across websites, apps, subscriptions, marketplaces, and custom payment flows. Stripe is also available within Shopify’s third-party payment-provider ecosystem.⁵


Stripe’s published standard UAE pricing is 2.9% + AED 1 for domestic cards, with an additional 1% for international cards and another 1% when currency conversion is required.⁶ There’s no standard setup or monthly account fee under its published UAE pricing.


Note:


You should confirm which cards and digital wallets are available through your specific Shopify setup. Shopify handles Apple Pay domain verification when Stripe is the provider, but you’ll still need to check that everything works with your store configuration.¹¹


Could be a fit if:


You want a globally established payment platform and expect to use Stripe for more than a basic Shopify checkout.


## Tap Payments


Tap Payments offers two Shopify plugin routes for businesses looking for regional payment methods:


- A native checkout option for supported cards and wallets


- Tap-hosted checkout page for other regional payment methods⁷


Depending on your setup, Tap says its plugins can support major cards, digital wallets, regional cards, BNPLoptions, and certain cash-based methods.⁷


Tap also offers payouts to supported bank accounts across the region and 24/7 live-chat support.⁷


Note:


Pricing and account features depend on the merchant, so ask Tap to confirm which methods you can activate through Shopify, the processing and international-card rates, refund and dispute charges, your settlement schedule, and which checkout route you’ll use.


Could be a fit if:


You sell to customers across the region and want a Shopify payment setup built around a broad range of regional payment methods.


## noon payments


noon payments offers a ready-made Shopify plugin designed to reduce the need for custom development. Beyond that plugin, its wider platform includes hosted checkout pages, APIs, mobile SDKs, and integrations for other e-commerce platforms.⁸


Depending on your agreement and integration, noon payments can also support cards, wallets, and BNPL options.⁸


Could be a fit if:


You want a regional provider and expect your payment setup to grow beyond a standard Shopify plugin over time.


## Paymob


Paymob is a regional payment provider with a pre-built Shopify integration and an embedded checkout option.⁹


Its wider platform includes online payment tools, payment links, APIs, mobile SDKs, and plugins for other e-commerce platforms.⁹


Could be a fit if:


You want a pre-built Shopify integration backed by a wider regional payment platform.


## Network International


Network International is a long-established regional payment provider that offers a dedicated Shopify plugin through its N-Genius Online gateway. The plugin is free to download and designed to work without a complex custom build.¹⁰


Beyond Shopify, Network International offers hosted payment pages, Pay By Link, virtual terminal payments, web and mobile SDKs, direct APIs, and alternative payment methods.¹⁰ It also has local operations across the Middle East and Africa, with 24/7 support.


Note:


Pricing and settlement terms are generally tailored to the merchant instead of presented as one standard public package. Ask for a proposal that clearly sets out how the Shopify plugin will work for your store, which payment methods and currencies you can offer, processing rates, and the support included.


Could be a fit if:


You want a regional acquiring provider with a Shopify plugin and a broad set of online payment tools.


## Final thoughts


Choosing the best UAE Shopify gateway provider would be simple if it just came down to the biggest global name, the lowest fees, or the most available features.


But there’s no shortcut around the details. You still should make sure these factors all make sense for your specific business situation:


- Compatibility with your Shopify plan and setup, and how easy it is to set up


- The real transaction cost and payout speed


- The range of payment methods and currencies it offers your customers


- Local support who understands the UAE market


- Support for the other channels you sell on now, or might add in the future
